passage.title: Report to the Harbour Board Inquiry: the loss of the SS Northern Star, 14 to 15 March 1912
paras: Introduction. This report sets out, in time order, the events that led to the loss of the passenger steamer SS Northern Star in the North Atlantic. It is based on the ship's log, which was recovered, and on the statements of 212 survivors. Its purpose is to explain what happened and to recommend changes so that such a loss is never repeated.

Departure (14 March, 10:00 am). The Northern Star left Liverpool for Halifax carrying 486 passengers and crew. She was regarded as modern and safe. However, she carried lifeboats for only 300 people, which met the rules of the time.

Warnings (14 March, 2:00 pm to 9:30 pm). During the afternoon, the wireless operator received three messages from nearby ships reporting ice. Only one of these reached the bridge. The captain ordered extra lookouts but did not reduce speed.

The collision (15 March, 1:40 am). At 1:40 am, a lookout sighted an iceberg directly ahead. The engines were reversed immediately; nevertheless, the ship struck the ice on her starboard side within forty seconds. Water entered five compartments.

The evacuation (1:50 am to 3:15 am). Shortly afterwards, distress signals were sent. Lifeboats were lowered, but several left only half full because passengers did not believe the ship would sink. Meanwhile, the steamer Carlotta changed course towards the signals.
Rescue (3:15 am to 6:00 am). The Northern Star sank at 3:15 am. The Carlotta arrived at 5:20 am and, by 6:00 am, had taken all 212 survivors aboard.
Findings. The inquiry finds that the loss was caused by excessive speed in an area of known ice, warnings that were not passed on, and too few lifeboats.
Recommendations. Every ship should carry lifeboat places for every person aboard; ice warnings must be taken to the bridge at once; lifeboat drills should take place on the first day of every voyage.
passage.source: An invented ship and inquiry, written for TGA as a model text. Every name and figure in it is made up.
